hypothesis: removing the length confound from the resolution curriculum would move the axis the nine previous candidates could not
result: REFUTED, and the intervention made the axis WORSE
why_it_failed: The fix targeted the wrong statistic. R-F4243 measured a COUNT SKEW — in how many pairs is the chosen answer shorter — and drove it from 0.90 to 0.55 by adding counter-examples on the other side of the chosen length. That does not make length uninformative; it turns a monotone confound into an INTERVAL one, which is easier to learn. Measured after the fact with R-F4247's separability metric, unique_live remained 100% separable by length (chosen 151-185 tight, rejected 49-76 and 316-2656 bimodal) and no_match 95%. The eval agrees with the geometry: resolution answers grew a median +306 characters and every lost resolution row was 'did not select the resolved company' — the model avoided the newly-rejected very-short answers and took shelter in the long list.
measurement_note: Against the stale pre-R-F4160 baseline the pod carried (155/168) this candidate reads +0 rather than -6. R-F4244 fixed that comparison; this run is the live demonstration of why it mattered.
next: Do NOT rebuild on the count-skew metric. R-F4247's gate now blocks BOTH the original curriculum and this one. A curriculum has to reach genuine length OVERLAP per branch, not a balanced count, before it is worth another cycle.
